b.5bb5407055:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

b.315a8a056a:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>D</c>eus tuórum mílitum
Sors, et córona, prǽmium,
Laudes canéntes Mártyris
Absólve nexu críminis.

<h>H</h>ic nempe mundi gáudia,
Et blanda fraudum pábula
Imbúta felle députans,
Pervénit ad cæléstia.

<h>P</h>œnas cucúrrit fórtiter,
Et sústulit viríliter,
Fundénsque pro te sánguinem,
Ætérna dona póssidet.

<h>O</h>b hoc precátu súpplici
Te póscimus, piíssime;
In hoc triúmpho Mártyris
Dimítte noxam sérvulis.

<h>L</h>aus et perénnis glória
Patri sit, atque Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
b.cafe880ee3:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>O</c> God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.

<h>H</h>e recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.

<h>B</h>ravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.

<h>W</h>ith humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.

<h>G</h>lory and praise for aye be done
To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Ghost, who reign on high,
One God, to all eternity.
Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Ecclesiástici
<r>Sir 51:1-7</r>
<n>1</n> Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Rex, et collaudábo te Deum Salvatórem meum.
<n>2</n> Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi,
<n>3</n> Et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne, a láqueo linguæ iníquæ et a lábiis operántium mendácium, et in conspéctu astántium factus es mihi adjútor.
<n>4</n> Et liberásti me secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ nóminis tui a rugiéntibus, præparátis ad escam:
<n>5</n> De mánibus quæréntium ánimam meam, et de portis tribulatiónum, quæ circumdedérunt me;
<n>6</n> A pressúra flammæ, quæ circúmdedit me, et in médio ignis non sum æstuáta;
<n>7</n> De altitúdine ventris ínferi, et a lingua coinquináta, et a verbo mendácii, a rege iníquo, et a lingua injústa.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Levíta Lauréntius bonum opus operátus est, qui per signum crucis cæcos illuminávit,
* Et thesáuros Ecclésiæ dedit paupéribus.
<r>℣.</r> Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus: justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
<r>℟.</r> Et thesáuros Ecclésiæ dedit paupéribus.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Ecclesiasticus
<r>Sir 51:1-7</r>
<n>1</n> A prayer of Jesus the son of Sirach. I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour.
<n>2</n> I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me.
<n>3</n> And hast preserved my body from destruction, from the snare of an unjust tongue, and from the lips of them that forge lies, and in the sight of them that stood by, thou hast been my helper.
<n>4</n> And thou hast delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of thy name, from them that did roar, prepared to devour.
<n>5</n> Out of the hands of them that sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions, which compassed me about:
<n>6</n> From the oppression of the flame which surrounded me, and in the midst of the fire I was not burnt.
<n>7</n> From the depth of the belly of hell, and from an unclean tongue, and from lying words, from an unjust king, and from a slanderous tongue:
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The Levite Lawrence wrought a good work, in that with the sign of the Cross he gave sight to the blind,
* And dispersed among the needy the riches of the Church.
<r>℣.</r> He hath dispersed, he hath given to the poor his righteousness endureth forever.
<r>℟.</r> And dispersed among the needy the riches of the Church.

<n>11</n> Memorátus sum misericórdiæ tuæ, Dómine, et operatiónis tuæ, quæ a sǽculo sunt:
<n>12</n> Quóniam éruis sustinéntes te, Dómine, et líberas eos de mánibus géntium.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.

<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, [in the year 295,] the holy Virgin Susanna, a damsel of noble birth, a niece to blessed Pope Caius. She was beheaded in the time of the Emperor Diocletian, and so gained the palm of martyrdom.
